module.title: Holiday Experiences & Travel Memories
module.objective: Recount past holiday experiences and travel memories in detail, including destinations, accommodation, activities, and impressions.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Sharing Holiday Stories
subModules.grammarFocus: Past Simple Tense (regular and irregular verbs, was/were for descriptions)
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Holiday destinations, accommodation, travel activities, feelings and impressions

content.summary: Welcome to your Reading Mission! In this lesson, you will read a short story about someone's holiday experience. You will practise understanding Past Simple sentences that describe where someone went, where they stayed, what they did, and how they felt. By the end of this mission, you will feel more confident reading short travel stories in English. Let's explore some wonderful holiday memories together!

linguisticTarget.grammar: Past Simple Tense — using Verb 2 forms (went, stayed, visited, bought, ate, saw) and was/were for descriptions and feelings in past holiday stories.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words related to holidays: destinations (beach, mountain, city), accommodation (hotel, room), activities (sightseeing, swimming, shopping), and impressions (incredible, delicious, cozy, beautiful).
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skimming for the main idea of a holiday story (Where did they go? Did they enjoy it?) and scanning for specific details (What did they do each day? What food did they eat?).

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a short A1 passage about a past holiday experience.
Identify key details including the destination, accommodation, activities, food, and the writer's feelings.
Recognize Past Simple verb forms (regular and irregular) and was/were in context.
Use time-sequence words (first, then, after that, finally) to follow the order of events in a story.
Build confidence reading short English texts about real-life travel experiences.

contextWarmup.prompt: Read this sentence: 'Last weekend, I visited a beautiful temple and took many photos.' What tense is this sentence in?
contextWarmup.explanation: Correct! The sentence uses Past Simple. The words 'visited' and 'took' are past forms of 'visit' and 'take'. The time marker 'Last weekend' also tells us this happened in the past. When we tell holiday stories, we use Past Simple because the holiday is finished.

rules: Use Past Simple verbs (Verb 2) to talk about completed holiday actions: 'I went to Bali.' 'We visited a temple.' 'She bought souvenirs.' All these actions are finished.
Use 'was' (singular) and 'were' (plural) to describe how things looked or felt during your holiday: 'The hotel was comfortable.' 'The beaches were beautiful.' 'The food was delicious.'

Follow the order of your story using time-sequence words: 'First, we arrived at the airport. Then, we checked in at the hotel. After that, we went to the beach. Finally, we had dinner at a local restaurant.'
Keep all verbs in Past Simple when telling one holiday story. Do not mix present and past tenses: Say 'I went and I saw' — not 'I went and I see.'
Look for time markers at the beginning of sentences to help you understand when things happened: 'Last summer', 'Two weeks ago', 'On the first day', 'In the evening'.

commonTrap.explanation: Many beginners forget to change ALL verbs to past tense when reading or writing a holiday story. They might understand 'went' is past, but then read 'buy' and think it is also past. Always check: does the verb look different from its base form? 'Buy' becomes 'bought', 'eat' becomes 'ate', 'see' becomes 'saw'. If the verb looks the same as the present form, it might be a mistake!
commonTrap.wrong: Last holiday, I went to the beach. I swim in the sea and eat fresh seafood.
commonTrap.correct: Last holiday, I went to the beach. I swam in the sea and ate fresh seafood.

sections.title: Reading Passage: My Trip to Lombok

content.context: Maya is writing a short blog post about her recent holiday to Lombok, Indonesia. She describes where she went, where she stayed, what she did, and how she felt about the trip.
content.text:
Last month, I went on holiday to Lombok with my best friend, Rina. Our flight from Jakarta was about two hours. We arrived in the afternoon and took a taxi to our hotel.

The hotel was small but very cozy. Our room had a nice view of the sea. On the first day, we went to the beach. The water was clear and warm. We swam and relaxed all day.

Then, on the second day, we went sightseeing. We visited a beautiful waterfall and took many photos. After that, we explored the local market and bought some souvenirs for our families.

On the last evening, we ate dinner at a small restaurant near the beach. The seafood was fresh and delicious. We watched a beautiful sunset while we ate.

The holiday was incredible. I really loved Lombok. I recommend it to everyone!

highlights.note: Past Simple of 'go' — irregular verb. Used to describe travelling to a place.
Past Simple of 'is' — used to describe how things looked or felt: 'The hotel was cozy.'
Past Simple of 'swim' — irregular verb. 'We swam in the sea.'
Past Simple of 'visit' — regular verb (add -ed). 'We visited a waterfall.'
Past Simple of 'buy' — irregular verb. 'We bought souvenirs.'
An adjective meaning warm and comfortable. 'The hotel was cozy.'
Small gifts you buy on holiday to remember the trip or give to friends.
The time in the evening when the sun goes down. 'We watched a beautiful sunset.'
An adjective meaning amazing or wonderful. 'The holiday was incredible.'
A time-sequence phrase that helps organise the story in order.

gistQuestion.prompt: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: Maya is telling us about her enjoyable past holiday in Lombok.
Maya is planning a future trip to Lombok with her friend.
Maya is complaining about a bad holiday experience.
gistQuestion.explanation: The passage is about Maya's past holiday in Lombok. She uses Past Simple verbs like 'went', 'visited', and 'ate' to describe what she did. She also says 'The holiday was incredible', which shows she enjoyed it. She is not planning a future trip or complaining — she is sharing a happy memory.

detailQuestions.prompt: Who did Maya go on holiday with?
detailQuestions.explanation: The passage says: 'I went on holiday to Lombok with my best friend, Rina.' This clearly tells us Maya travelled with her best friend. There is no mention of family or classmates joining the trip.

detailQuestions.prompt: What did Maya and Rina do on the second day?
options: They went sightseeing, visited a waterfall, explored a market, and bought souvenirs.
They went to the beach and swam all day.
They ate dinner at a restaurant and watched the sunset.
detailQuestions.explanation: The passage says: 'On the second day, we went sightseeing. We visited a beautiful waterfall and took many photos. After that, we explored the local market and bought some souvenirs.' Swimming at the beach was on the first day, and dinner at the restaurant was on the last evening.

detailQuestions.prompt: How does Maya describe the hotel?
options: It was small but very cozy, with a nice sea view.
It was big and expensive with a swimming pool.
detailQuestions.explanation: Maya writes: 'The hotel was small but very cozy. Our room had a nice view of the sea.' She does not mention a swimming pool, and she describes the hotel positively — not as old or uncomfortable.

detailQuestions.prompt: What did Maya eat on the last evening?
options: Fresh and delicious seafood at a small restaurant near the beach.
Traditional food at the hotel restaurant.
Street food at the local market.
detailQuestions.explanation: The passage says: 'We ate dinner at a small restaurant near the beach. The seafood was fresh and delicious.' Maya does not mention eating at the hotel or at the market.

questions.question: According to the passage, how long was the flight from Jakarta to Lombok?
questions.answer: About two hours.
questions.explanation: Maya writes: 'Our flight from Jakarta was about two hours.' This is a specific detail you can find by scanning the first paragraph of the passage.

questions.question: Which sentence from the passage uses Past Simple correctly to describe a holiday activity?
options: 'We visited a beautiful waterfall and took many photos.'
'We visit a beautiful waterfall and take many photos.'
'We are visiting a beautiful waterfall and taking many photos.'
questions.answer: 'We visited a beautiful waterfall and took many photos.'
questions.explanation: The first option is correct because 'visited' (past of 'visit') and 'took' (past of 'take') are both in Past Simple. The second option uses present tense, and the third uses present continuous — neither is correct for a finished holiday story.

questions.question: In the passage, Maya says 'The water was clear and warm.' What does 'was' tell us?
options: It describes how the water looked and felt in the past.
It describes how the water looks and feels right now.
It describes how the water will look in the future.
questions.answer: It describes how the water looked and felt in the past.
questions.explanation: 'Was' is the Past Simple form of 'is'. Maya is describing the water during her past holiday, not right now or in the future. We use 'was/were' to describe conditions and feelings in the past.

questions.question: What time-sequence words does Maya use to organise her story? Choose the best answer.
options: 'On the first day', 'Then, on the second day', 'After that', 'On the last evening'
questions.answer: 'On the first day', 'Then, on the second day', 'After that', 'On the last evening'
questions.explanation: Maya uses time-sequence phrases like 'On the first day', 'Then, on the second day', 'After that', and 'On the last evening' to put her holiday events in order. These phrases help the reader follow the story from beginning to end.

questions.question: Maya writes: 'I recommend it to everyone!' What does 'recommend' mean in this sentence?
options: She suggests that other people should visit Lombok because it is wonderful.
She warns other people not to go to Lombok.
She asks other people to help her plan another trip.
questions.answer: She suggests that other people should visit Lombok because it is wonderful.
questions.explanation: 'Recommend' means to suggest something good to other people. Maya loved her holiday, so she recommends Lombok — she thinks everyone should visit. She is not warning people or asking for help.

questions.question: Read this sentence: 'We explored the local market and bought some souvenirs for our families.' What are the Past Simple verbs?
questions.answer: 'explored' and 'bought'
questions.explanation: 'Explored' is the Past Simple of 'explore' (regular: add -ed). 'Bought' is the Past Simple of 'buy' (irregular). 'Explore' and 'buy' are base forms (present), and 'local' and 'some' are not verbs at all.

questions.question: Which sentence best summarises Maya's feelings about her holiday?
options: She thought the holiday was incredible and she loved Lombok.
She thought the holiday was boring and too short.
She was unhappy because the hotel was uncomfortable.
questions.answer: She thought the holiday was incredible and she loved Lombok.
questions.explanation: At the end of the passage, Maya writes: 'The holiday was incredible. I really loved Lombok. I recommend it to everyone!' These sentences clearly show that she had a very positive experience. She does not say the holiday was boring, and she describes the hotel as cozy — not uncomfortable.

content.summary: In this listening mission, you will hear two colleagues, Sarah and Tom, talking about their weekend holidays at the office. Tom went on a trip to Yogyakarta and tells Sarah about his hotel, the places he visited, the souvenirs he bought, and the food he ate. Sarah stayed at home and relaxed. Listen carefully for past tense verbs like 'stayed', 'visited', 'bought', and adjectives that describe experiences like 'incredible', 'amazing', and 'delicious'. Pay attention to how speakers ask about holiday experiences using questions like 'How was your trip?' and 'What did you do there?' These are very common patterns when people share travel memories.
learningObjectives: Understand simple past tense verbs used to describe holiday activities (visited, stayed, bought).
Identify key details about a trip: destination, accommodation, activities, souvenirs, and food.
Recognize common questions and responses for sharing travel experiences.
Understand adjectives used to describe holiday impressions (incredible, amazing, delicious, cozy).

keyPhrases.note: A very common question to ask someone about their holiday or travel experience. Use 'was' because the trip is finished (past tense).

keyPhrases.phrase: We stayed at a cozy hotel.
keyPhrases.meaning: Kami menginap di hotel yang nyaman.
keyPhrases.note: 'Stayed at' is used to talk about where you slept during a trip. 'Cozy' means warm, comfortable, and pleasant.
'Visited' is the past tense of 'visit'. Use it to talk about places you went to see during a holiday.
'Views' means what you can see from a place, like scenery. 'Amazing' is a strong positive adjective meaning very wonderful.
A yes/no question in the past tense using 'did'. 'Souvenirs' are things you buy to remember a trip.
'Delicious' means the food tasted very good. This is a common way to share a positive impression about food during a trip.
'Should' is used here to give a friendly suggestion or recommendation. 'Next time' means in the future.

connectedSpeech.note: In natural speech, 'was' reduces from /wɒz/ to a weak /wəz/, and 'your' shortens to /jər/. The stress falls on 'weekend' and 'trip'.
'Was' weakens to /wəz/ in fast speech. The main stress is on the second syllable of 'incredible': in-CRED-ible. The final syllable often reduces.
'What did' blends together so 'what' and 'did' sound almost like one word: /wɒdɪd/. 'You' reduces to /jə/.
'Did you' merges into /dɪdʒə/ in fast natural speech. This is very common in everyday English conversation.
'That' reduces to /ðət/ with a schwa. The 'd' in 'sounds' can be barely heard, making it sound like /saʊnz/.

sections.title: Audio Dialogue: Holiday Stories at the Office

content.context: Sarah and Tom meet at the office on Monday morning after the weekend. They talk about their holidays. Tom went on a trip to Yogyakarta, and Sarah stayed at home. They share their experiences and feelings about the weekend.
content.audioPrompt: Listen carefully to the following dialogue between Sarah and Tom. Pay attention to the past tense verbs and the adjectives they use to describe their holiday experiences.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Hi Tom! How was your weekend trip to Yogyakarta?
lines.translation: Hai Tom! Bagaimana perjalanan akhir pekanmu ke Yogyakarta?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It was incredible! We stayed at a cozy hotel near Malioboro Street.
lines.translation: Luar biasa! Kami menginap di hotel yang nyaman dekat Jalan Malioboro.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: That sounds great! What did you do there?
lines.translation: Kedengarannya bagus! Apa yang kamu lakukan di sana?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We visited Borobudur Temple and Prambanan. The views were amazing!
lines.translation: Kami mengunjungi Candi Borobudur dan Prambanan. Pemandangannya menakjubkan!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Wow! Did you buy any souvenirs?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Yes, I bought some batik and traditional snacks. The food was delicious too!
lines.translation: Ya, saya membeli beberapa batik dan makanan ringan tradisional. Makanannya juga lezat!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: That's wonderful! Did you take many photos?
lines.translation: Itu luar biasa! Apakah kamu mengambil banyak foto?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Oh yes! I took so many photos at the temples. I can show you later.
lines.translation: Oh ya! Saya mengambil banyak sekali foto di candi-candi. Saya bisa tunjukkan nanti.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I'm so jealous! My holiday was just at home, relaxing.
lines.translation: Aku iri! Liburanku hanya di rumah, bersantai.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's nice too! Sometimes we need rest. You should visit Yogyakarta next time!
lines.translation: Itu juga bagus! Kadang kita perlu istirahat. Kamu harus mengunjungi Yogyakarta lain kali!

content.summary: In this lesson, you will learn how to write about your holiday experiences and travel memories. You will use the Past Simple tense to talk about things you did. You will use 'was' and 'were' to describe places and feelings. You will also use time connectors like 'first', 'then', 'after that', and 'finally' to tell your story in order. Let's build your holiday story step by step!

blueprintItems.title: Say Where You Went and When
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + went to + Place + Time Expression
blueprintItems.example: I went to Bali last summer.

blueprintItems.title: Describe Where You Stayed and How It Was
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + stayed at/in + Place. + It was / The [noun] was/were + Adjective.
blueprintItems.example: I stayed at a small hotel. It was clean and comfortable.

blueprintItems.title: Tell What You Did Using Time Connectors
blueprintItems.formula: First, + Subject + Verb2. Then, + Subject + Verb2. After that, + Subject + Verb2. Finally, + Subject + Verb2.
blueprintItems.example: First, I visited the beach. Then, I tried local food. After that, I bought some souvenirs. Finally, I took many photos.

blueprintItems.title: Share Your Feelings About the Holiday
blueprintItems.formula: It was + Adjective. / I was + Adjective. / The holiday was + Adjective.
blueprintItems.example: It was an amazing holiday. I was very happy.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize the names of places, cities, and countries.
mechanicsRules.badExample: i went to bali and visited lombok.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I went to Bali and visited Lombok.
mechanicsRules.why: Place names are proper nouns. They always start with a capital letter. The word 'I' is also always capitalized.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a period (.) at the end of every sentence. Use a comma (,) after time connectors like 'First', 'Then', 'After that', and 'Finally'.
mechanicsRules.badExample: first we went to the beach then we had lunch
mechanicsRules.goodExample: First, we went to the beach. Then, we had lunch.
mechanicsRules.why: A period shows where one sentence ends. A comma after a time connector gives the reader a small pause and makes the sentence easier to read.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use Past Simple verbs (Verb 2) when you write about finished holiday actions. Do not mix present and past tense in the same story.
mechanicsRules.badExample: I go to the market and I bought a hat.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I went to the market and I bought a hat.
mechanicsRules.why: Your holiday already happened, so all verbs must be in the past tense. 'Go' is present tense. 'Went' is the correct past tense form.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use 'was' with I, he, she, it, and singular nouns. Use 'were' with you, we, they, and plural nouns.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The beaches was beautiful. The hotel were nice.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The beaches were beautiful. The hotel was nice.
mechanicsRules.why: 'Beaches' is plural, so it needs 'were'. 'Hotel' is singular, so it needs 'was'. Matching the correct form is important for clear writing.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: My Best Holiday
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write a short paragraph (at least 4 sentences) about a holiday you had. Tell where you went, where you stayed, what you did, and how you felt. Use Past Simple verbs (went, stayed, visited, bought, ate). Use time connectors (first, then, after that, finally) to put your story in order.
guidedLabChallenges.example: I went to Bandung last year. I stayed at my grandmother's house. First, I visited a tea garden. Then, I ate delicious local food at a restaurant. After that, I bought souvenirs for my friends. Finally, I went home. It was a wonderful holiday. I was very happy.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: I went to ... last ... . I stayed at ... . First, I ... . Then, I ... .

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: A Postcard to My Friend
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Imagine you are on holiday. Write a short postcard to your friend. Tell your friend where you are, what you did yesterday, and what you think about the place. Use Past Simple for yesterday's activities. Use 'was/were' to describe the place. Write at least 5 sentences.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Dear Rina, I am in Bali now! Yesterday, I went to a beautiful beach. The water was warm and the sand was white. I swam in the sea and I ate fresh seafood. After that, I watched the sunset. It was so beautiful! The hotel is nice and the people here are very friendly. I bought a small gift for you. See you soon! From, Dina.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Write 3 to 4 sentences about a place you visited on holiday. Tell where you went, when you went, and what you saw there. Use Past Simple verbs.
practicumQuestions.criteria: Uses Past Simple correctly (went, visited, saw). Includes a place name with a capital letter. Includes a time expression (last week, last year, in January). Each sentence ends with a period. At least 3 complete sentences.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: I went to Jakarta last January. I visited the National Museum with my family. We saw many old things and beautiful art. It was very interesting.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Describe the hotel or place where you stayed on a holiday. Write 3 to 4 sentences. Use 'was' or 'were' to describe it.
practicumQuestions.criteria: Uses 'was' with singular nouns and 'were' with plural nouns correctly. Includes at least 2 adjectives to describe the place (clean, big, comfortable, friendly). Proper capitalization and punctuation. At least 3 complete sentences.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: I stayed at a small hotel in Malang. The room was clean and comfortable. The beds were soft. The staff were very friendly and helpful.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Write a short holiday story (5 to 7 sentences). Use time connectors (first, then, after that, finally) to tell what you did in order. Include where you went, what activities you did, and how you felt about the holiday.
practicumQuestions.criteria: Uses at least 3 different time connectors (first, then, after that, finally). All verbs about past activities are in Past Simple. Includes a feeling sentence using 'was' (e.g., 'It was amazing', 'I was happy'). Proper capitalization of place names, 'I', and sentence beginnings. Commas after time connectors. At least 5 complete sentences.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: Last month, I went to Labuan Bajo with my family. We stayed at a hotel near the sea. First, we took a boat to Komodo Island. We saw big Komodo dragons there. Then, we went snorkeling. The water was very clear and the fish were colorful. After that, we ate fresh fish at a local restaurant. Finally, we watched the sunset from the beach. It was the best holiday. I was so happy and I want to go back again.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Sharing Your Holiday Experiences & Travel Memories

content.summary: In this speaking lab, you will learn how to talk about your past holiday experiences clearly and confidently. You will practise telling someone where you went, where you stayed, what you did, and how you felt about your trip. We will focus on using simple past tense verbs correctly, stressing the right syllables in travel vocabulary, and using natural rising and falling intonation when sharing stories and answering questions about your holiday.
content.audioGuidance: When you talk about your holiday, speak slowly and clearly. Use falling intonation at the end of statements like 'I went to Bali.' Use rising intonation for yes/no questions like 'Did you enjoy it?' Pay special attention to the past tense '-ed' endings: 'visited' has three syllables (VI-si-ted), but 'stayed' has only one syllable (stayed). Practise linking words smoothly, for example 'went to' sounds like 'went-to' with a soft connection.

pillars.name: Past Tense Pronunciation
pillars.target: Correctly pronounce regular past tense verb endings (-ed)
pillars.explanation: The '-ed' ending has three different sounds: /t/ after voiceless sounds (like 'walked'), /d/ after voiced sounds (like 'stayed'), and /ɪd/ after 't' or 'd' sounds (like 'visited'). Practise each type so your holiday stories sound natural and clear.

pillars.name: Storytelling Intonation
pillars.target: Use natural rising and falling pitch when telling a story
pillars.explanation: When you tell a story about your holiday, your voice should go up slightly in the middle of a list ('We went to the beach, visited a temple, and tried surfing') and come down at the end. This makes your story sound interesting and easy to follow.

pillars.name: Travel Vocabulary Stress
pillars.target: Stress the correct syllable in travel-related words
pillars.explanation: Many travel words have specific stress patterns. For example, 'HOtel' is stressed on the second syllable (ho-TEL), 'BEAUtiful' is stressed on the first syllable (BEAU-ti-ful), and 'inCREdible' is stressed on the second syllable (in-CRED-i-ble). Getting the stress right helps people understand you.

pillars.name: Descriptive Expression
pillars.target: Use simple adjectives and phrases to describe holiday impressions
pillars.explanation: To make your holiday story interesting, use descriptive words like 'amazing', 'beautiful', 'cozy', 'friendly', and 'incredible'. Practise saying short opinion phrases like 'It was wonderful!', 'The view was breathtaking!', and 'I had a great time!' with enthusiasm in your voice.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: In 'hotel', the stress is on the second syllable: ho-TEL. When we add 'room' to make 'hotel room', both 'TEL' and 'room' carry stress, but 'TEL' remains the primary stress in the first word.

In 'beautiful', the stress is on the first syllable: BEAU-ti-ful. When it becomes 'beautifully', the stress stays on the first syllable, but the word is longer. Practise keeping the strong BEAU sound at the start.

In 'visit', the stress is on the first syllable: VI-sit. When we add '-ed' to make 'visited', it becomes three syllables (VI-si-ted), but the stress stays on the first syllable. The '-ted' ending is pronounced as a separate syllable because 'visit' ends in a 't' sound.

In 'incredible', the stress is on the second syllable: in-CRED-i-ble. When it becomes 'incredibly', the stress stays on 'CRED'. Make sure you say the 'CRED' part louder and longer than the other syllables.

drills.targetText: I went to Bali last week.
drills.focus: Simple past tense 'went' and smooth sentence flow
drills.hint: Say 'went' clearly with a short 'e' sound. Link 'went to' smoothly so it sounds like 'went-to'. Drop your voice at the end because this is a statement.

drills.targetText: We stayed at a small hotel near the beach.
drills.phonetic: /wiː steɪd ət ə smɔːl hoʊˈtɛl nɪr ðə biːtʃ/
drills.focus: Past tense 'stayed' (/steɪd/) and word stress in 'hotel'
drills.hint: Say 'stayed' as one syllable: /steɪd/. Remember 'hotel' is stressed on the second syllable: ho-TEL. The word 'beach' ends with a 'ch' sound — push air out softly.
Say 'visited' with three syllables: VI-si-ted. The stress is on 'VI'. Do not skip the '-ted' ending — it is a separate syllable because 'visit' ends in a 't' sound.
Show excitement in your voice! Stress 'CRED' in 'incredible' and 'LU' in 'absolutely'. Let your voice rise slightly on 'incredible' and then fall at the end to show strong feeling.

drills.targetText: My favourite part was watching the sunset.
drills.phonetic: /maɪ ˈfeɪvərɪt pɑːrt wɒz ˈwɒtʃɪŋ ðə ˈsʌnˌsɛt/
drills.focus: Stress on 'favourite' and 'sunset', natural sentence rhythm
drills.hint: Stress the first syllable of 'favourite': FAV-ou-rite. Also stress the first part of 'sunset': SUN-set. Pause slightly after 'was' to create a natural rhythm.
This is a yes/no question, so your voice should go UP at the end on 'holiday'. Stress 'JOY' in 'enjoy' and 'HOL' in 'holiday'.

roleplay.context: You have just come back from a holiday. You meet Mr. Khoirul at school, and he wants to hear all about your trip. Tell him where you went, where you stayed, what activities you did, and what your favourite part of the holiday was. Use simple past tense and descriptive words to share your experience.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Hello! Welcome back! I heard you went on holiday last week. Where did you go?
turns.translation: Halo! Selamat datang kembali! Saya dengar kamu pergi liburan minggu lalu. Ke mana kamu pergi?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Hi Mr. Khoirul! Yes, I went to Bali. It was my first time there!
turns.translation: Hai Pak Khoirul! Ya, saya pergi ke Bali. Itu pertama kalinya saya ke sana!

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That's wonderful! Bali is beautiful. Where did you stay? At a hotel or a villa?
turns.translation: Itu luar biasa! Bali itu indah. Kamu menginap di mana? Di hotel atau villa?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: We stayed at a small hotel near Kuta Beach. It was cozy and the staff were very friendly.
turns.translation: Kami menginap di hotel kecil dekat Pantai Kuta. Hotelnya nyaman dan stafnya sangat ramah.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Nice choice! What activities did you do during your holiday?
turns.translation: Pilihan yang bagus! Aktivitas apa yang kamu lakukan selama liburan?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: We went to the beach every day, visited Tanah Lot Temple, and tried surfing. We also went shopping for souvenirs.
turns.translation: Kami pergi ke pantai setiap hari, mengunjungi Pura Tanah Lot, dan mencoba berselancar. Kami juga pergi berbelanja oleh-oleh.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Sounds like you had an amazing time! What was your favourite part of the trip?
turns.translation: Kedengarannya kamu bersenang-senang! Apa bagian favoritmu dari perjalanan itu?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: My favourite part was watching the sunset at Tanah Lot. It was absolutely incredible! The view was breathtaking.
turns.translation: Bagian favorit saya adalah melihat matahari terbenam di Tanah Lot. Itu benar-benar luar biasa! Pemandangannya menakjubkan.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Tell a short story about a holiday you took. Describe where you went, what you did, and how you felt. Speak for about 30 seconds. Use simple past tense.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please tell me about a holiday you remember. Where did you go? What did you do there? And how did you feel about the trip? Take your time and tell me the story.
storyPoints: Tell where you went on holiday and who you went with.
Describe two or three activities you did during the holiday.
Share how you felt about the holiday and what your favourite part was.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I went to Bali with my family. We visited temples, went to the beach, and tried surfing. My favourite part was watching the sunset. It was an amazing holiday!
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ wɛnt tə ˈbɑːli wɪð maɪ ˈfæmɪli. wiː ˈvɪzɪtɪd ˈtɛmpəlz, wɛnt tə ðə biːtʃ, ænd traɪd ˈsɜːrfɪŋ. maɪ ˈfeɪvərɪt pɑːrt wɒz ˈwɒtʃɪŋ ðə ˈsʌnˌsɛt. ɪt wɒz ən əˈmeɪzɪŋ ˈhɒlɪdeɪ/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use past tense verbs: 'went', 'visited', 'tried', 'was'. Describe your feelings with adjectives like 'amazing', 'beautiful', or 'incredible'.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This storytelling task practises your ability to narrate a past holiday experience in a logical order. Start with where you went, then describe activities, and finish with your feelings. Using past tense correctly and descriptive adjectives makes your story clear and interesting.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Tell a short story about the best hotel or place you stayed at during a holiday. Describe the place, what it looked like, and why you liked it. Speak for about 30 seconds.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: I would love to hear about a place you stayed at during a holiday. What kind of place was it? What did it look like? Why did you like staying there? Please tell me the story.
storyPoints: Describe what kind of accommodation you stayed at (hotel, villa, homestay) and where it was located.
Tell what the place looked like — was it big or small, old or new, cozy or modern?
Explain why you liked staying there and mention something special about it.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: We stayed at a small hotel near the beach. The rooms were clean and cozy. The staff were very friendly and helpful. I liked it because I could see the ocean from my window. It was a wonderful place to stay!
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /wiː steɪd ət ə smɔːl hoʊˈtɛl nɪr ðə biːtʃ. ðə ruːmz wɜːr kliːn ænd ˈkoʊzi. ðə stæf wɜːr ˈvɛri ˈfrɛndli ænd ˈhɛlpfʊl. aɪ laɪkt ɪt bɪˈkɒz aɪ kʊd siː ðə ˈoʊʃən frɒm maɪ ˈwɪndoʊ/
practicumQuestions.hint: Describe the place using adjectives: 'small', 'clean', 'cozy', 'friendly'. Use 'was' and 'were' to describe things in the past. Say why you liked it with 'because'.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This task helps you practise describing accommodation using simple adjectives and past tense. Organising your description from general (type and location) to specific (details and feelings) makes your story easy to follow.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are calling Mr. Khoirul to tell him about your holiday in Yogyakarta. He will ask you questions about your trip. Answer his questions using simple past tense and describe your experiences.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Ring ring! Hello, this is Mr. Khoirul speaking. I heard you just came back from Yogyakarta! Tell me all about it. Where did you stay and what did you do?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You have just returned from a three-day holiday in Yogyakarta. You stayed at a guesthouse near Malioboro Street. You visited Borobudur Temple, tried local food like gudeg, and bought batik souvenirs. You had a wonderful time and want to share your experience with Mr. Khoirul over the phone.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is your friendly English tutor who is curious about your holiday. He will ask follow-up questions about your accommodation, activities, food, and favourite moments. He speaks slowly and encouragingly.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I went to Yogyakarta for three days. I stayed at a guesthouse near Malioboro Street. I visited Borobudur Temple and it was amazing. I also tried gudeg and bought batik souvenirs.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ wɛnt tə ˌjɒɡjəˈkɑːrtə fɔːr θriː deɪz. aɪ steɪd ət ə ˈɡɛsthaʊs nɪr ˌmɑːliəˈbɒroʊ striːt/
practicumQuestions.hint: Answer each question with a full sentence. For example: 'I stayed at a guesthouse.' Use past tense: went, stayed, visited, tried, bought.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises real conversation about holidays. Answering questions with full sentences and past tense verbs helps you communicate your travel experiences clearly and naturally.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are at a travel agency. Mr. Khoirul is the travel agent. Tell him about a past holiday you enjoyed and ask him to help you plan a similar trip. Describe what you liked about your last holiday.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Good morning! Welcome to Happy Travel Agency. I am Mr. Khoirul. How can I help you today? Have you travelled anywhere nice before?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are visiting a travel agency because you want to go on another holiday. You had a great holiday in Lombok last year and you want to go somewhere similar. You need to tell the travel agent about your past trip — where you went, what you did, and what you enjoyed — so he can suggest a new destination.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is a friendly travel agent at Happy Travel Agency. He listens carefully to your past holiday experience and asks questions to understand what kind of holiday you enjoy. He speaks in simple, clear English.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Last year, I went to Lombok. I stayed at a beach resort. I went snorkelling and visited beautiful waterfalls. I really enjoyed the quiet beaches. Can you help me find a similar place?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /lɑːst jɪr aɪ wɛnt tə ˈlɒmbɒk. aɪ steɪd ət ə biːtʃ rɪˈzɔːrt. aɪ wɛnt ˈsnɔːrkəlɪŋ ænd ˈvɪzɪtɪd ˈbjuːtɪfʊl ˈwɔːtərfɔːlz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Start by telling about your past trip: 'Last year, I went to...' Then describe activities: 'I went snorkelling.' Finally, ask for help: 'Can you help me find...?'
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay combines talking about past experiences with making a request. It practises past tense narration and polite question forms, both essential for real-world travel conversations.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You meet Mr. Khoirul at a coffee shop. He asks about your recent weekend trip. Tell him about your short holiday — where you went, what you saw, and whether you recommend it.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Hey there! Sit down, have some coffee. I saw your photos on social media — you went somewhere nice this weekend! Tell me about it. Where did you go?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You went on a short weekend trip to Bandung. You visited a tea plantation, ate local street food, and stayed at a small inn in the mountains. The weather was cool and refreshing. You took many photos and had a relaxing time. Now you are telling Mr. Khoirul about it at a coffee shop.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is your friend and English tutor. You meet him casually at a coffee shop. He is interested in your weekend trip and asks friendly questions about the destination, food, weather, and your overall experience. He is relaxed and encouraging.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I went to Bandung this weekend. I visited a tea plantation in the mountains. The weather was cool and nice. I ate delicious street food and stayed at a small inn. It was very relaxing. I recommend it!
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ wɛnt tə ˈbændʌŋ ðɪs ˈwiːkˌɛnd. aɪ ˈvɪzɪtɪd ə tiː plænˈteɪʃən ɪn ðə ˈmaʊntɪnz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Describe the place, the weather, and the food. Use adjectives like 'cool', 'delicious', 'relaxing'. End by saying if you recommend it: 'I recommend it!'
practicumQuestions.explanation: This casual roleplay practises informal storytelling about a short trip. Using descriptive adjectives and giving a recommendation at the end makes your conversation natural and engaging.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are video-calling Mr. Khoirul from your holiday. Describe what you can see around you, what you did today, and what you plan to do tomorrow. Use present and past tense.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Hello! Oh wow, you are calling me from your holiday! That is so nice! What can you see around you right now? And what did you do today?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are on holiday at a beach in Labuan Bajo. You are video-calling Mr. Khoirul in the evening. Today you went on a boat trip to see Komodo dragons, swam in crystal clear water, and had fresh seafood for lunch. Tomorrow you plan to go snorkelling at Pink Beach. You are sitting on the hotel terrace with a beautiful ocean view.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is your English tutor. He is excited to receive your video call from your holiday. He asks about what you see now, what you did today, and your plans for tomorrow. He reacts with enthusiasm and asks follow-up questions.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Right now I can see the ocean from my hotel terrace. It is beautiful! Today I went on a boat trip and saw Komodo dragons. I also swam in the sea and ate fresh seafood. Tomorrow I plan to go snorkelling at Pink Beach.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /raɪt naʊ aɪ kæn siː ðə ˈoʊʃən frɒm maɪ hoʊˈtɛl ˈtɛrəs. ɪt ɪz ˈbjuːtɪfʊl. təˈdeɪ aɪ wɛnt ɒn ə boʊt trɪp ænd sɔː kəˈmoʊdoʊ ˈdræɡənz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use present tense for what you see now: 'I can see...' Use past tense for today: 'I went...', 'I saw...' Use 'plan to' for tomorrow: 'I plan to go...'
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises mixing present and past tense in a natural conversation. Describing your current surroundings, today's activities, and tomorrow's plans is a common real-life situation when sharing holiday updates.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following travel vocabulary word clearly. Focus on correct pronunciation and stress.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say this travel word clearly. Think about which syllable is stressed. The word is: 'accommodation'. It means the place where you stay during a holiday, like a hotel or a guesthouse.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /əˌkɒməˈdeɪʃən/
practicumQuestions.hint: This word has five syllables: a-com-mo-DA-tion. The stress is on the fourth syllable 'DA'. Say it slowly first: a-com-mo-DAY-shun, then say it at normal speed.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The word 'accommodation' is important for talking about holidays. It means the place where you sleep, such as a hotel, villa, or guesthouse. The main stress falls on the fourth syllable: a-com-mo-DA-tion. Practising long words by breaking them into syllables helps you pronounce them correctly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence using the correct past tense form. Pay attention to the irregular past tense verbs.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say this sentence about a holiday activity. Make sure you use the correct past tense. Listen carefully: 'We went to the beach and swam in the sea.' Now you say it.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: We went to the beach and swam in the sea.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /wiː wɛnt tə ðə biːtʃ ænd swæm ɪn ðə siː/
practicumQuestions.hint: Remember: 'go' becomes 'went' in the past, and 'swim' becomes 'swam' in the past. These are irregular verbs — they do not use '-ed'. Say 'went' with a short 'e' sound and 'swam' with a short 'a' sound.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill practises irregular past tense verbs commonly used in holiday stories. 'Go → went' and 'swim → swam' are irregular verbs that do not follow the regular '-ed' pattern. Knowing these forms is essential for telling stories about past holidays naturally.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following pair of words. Notice how the syllable stress changes between the base word and the longer form. Practise both clearly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Listen to the stress difference between these two words. First: 'PHOtograph' — stress on the first syllable. Second: 'phoTOGraphy' — stress on the second syllable. Now you say both words. Notice how the stress moves!
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈfoʊtəɡrɑːf/ vs /fəˈtɒɡrəfi/
practicumQuestions.hint: In 'photograph', stress the first syllable: PHO-to-graph. In 'photography', the stress shifts to the second syllable: pho-TOG-ra-phy. The vowel sounds also change when the stress moves. Practise saying both words one after the other to feel the shift.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This stress drill shows how adding a suffix can shift the stressed syllable. 'PHOtograph' has stress on the first syllable, but 'phoTOGraphy' shifts the stress to the second syllable. This pattern is common in English and is very relevant for holiday vocabulary, since we often talk about taking photographs and photography during trips.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following two sentences. The first is a statement with falling intonation. The second is a yes/no question with rising intonation. Practise the difference clearly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Listen to the intonation difference. Statement with falling intonation: 'You enjoyed your holiday.' ↘ Your voice goes DOWN at the end. Now the question with rising intonation: 'Did you enjoy your holiday?' ↗ Your voice goes UP at the end. Now you say both!
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: You enjoyed your holiday. ↘ / Did you enjoy your holiday? ↗
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /juː ɪnˈdʒɔɪd jɔːr ˈhɒlɪdeɪ ↘/ vs /dɪd juː ɪnˈdʒɔɪd jɔːr ˈhɒlɪdeɪ ↗/
practicumQuestions.hint: For the statement, let your voice fall down naturally at the end on 'holiday' — this shows you are giving information. For the question, let your voice rise up at the end on 'holiday' — this shows you are asking and expecting a yes or no answer. Exaggerate the rise and fall at first to practise.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill practises the fundamental difference between falling intonation (for statements) and rising intonation (for yes/no questions). In English, statements about past experiences use falling intonation to sound confident and complete. Yes/no questions use rising intonation to signal that you are asking and waiting for an answer. Mastering this difference makes your spoken English sound much more natural.

subModules.title: Final Mission: Unit 3 Comprehensive Assessment (55 Soal)

content.summary: Ujian akhir unit resmi untuk Holiday Experiences & Travel Memories. Menguji 4 kompetensi terintegrasi (Reading 15 soal, Listening 15 soal, Writing 10 soal, Speaking 15 soal) untuk menghasilkan scorecard nilai resmi per unit.

reading.question: According to the passage, how long was the flight from Jakarta to Lombok?
reading.explanation: Maya writes: 'Our flight from Jakarta was about two hours.' This is a specific detail you can find by scanning the first paragraph of the passage.

reading.question: Which sentence from the passage uses Past Simple correctly to describe a holiday activity?
options: 'We visited a beautiful waterfall and took many photos.'
'We visit a beautiful waterfall and take many photos.'
'We are visiting a beautiful waterfall and taking many photos.'
reading.answer: 'We visited a beautiful waterfall and took many photos.'
reading.explanation: The first option is correct because 'visited' (past of 'visit') and 'took' (past of 'take') are both in Past Simple. The second option uses present tense, and the third uses present continuous — neither is correct for a finished holiday story.

reading.question: In the passage, Maya says 'The water was clear and warm.' What does 'was' tell us?
options: It describes how the water looked and felt in the past.
It describes how the water looks and feels right now.
It describes how the water will look in the future.
reading.answer: It describes how the water looked and felt in the past.
reading.explanation: 'Was' is the Past Simple form of 'is'. Maya is describing the water during her past holiday, not right now or in the future. We use 'was/were' to describe conditions and feelings in the past.

reading.question: What time-sequence words does Maya use to organise her story? Choose the best answer.
options: 'On the first day', 'Then, on the second day', 'After that', 'On the last evening'
reading.answer: 'On the first day', 'Then, on the second day', 'After that', 'On the last evening'
reading.explanation: Maya uses time-sequence phrases like 'On the first day', 'Then, on the second day', 'After that', and 'On the last evening' to put her holiday events in order. These phrases help the reader follow the story from beginning to end.

reading.question: Maya writes: 'I recommend it to everyone!' What does 'recommend' mean in this sentence?
options: She suggests that other people should visit Lombok because it is wonderful.
She warns other people not to go to Lombok.
She asks other people to help her plan another trip.
reading.answer: She suggests that other people should visit Lombok because it is wonderful.
reading.explanation: 'Recommend' means to suggest something good to other people. Maya loved her holiday, so she recommends Lombok — she thinks everyone should visit. She is not warning people or asking for help.

reading.question: Read this sentence: 'We explored the local market and bought some souvenirs for our families.' What are the Past Simple verbs?
reading.explanation: 'Explored' is the Past Simple of 'explore' (regular: add -ed). 'Bought' is the Past Simple of 'buy' (irregular). 'Explore' and 'buy' are base forms (present), and 'local' and 'some' are not verbs at all.

reading.question: Which sentence best summarises Maya's feelings about her holiday?
options: She thought the holiday was incredible and she loved Lombok.
She thought the holiday was boring and too short.
She was unhappy because the hotel was uncomfortable.
reading.answer: She thought the holiday was incredible and she loved Lombok.
reading.explanation: At the end of the passage, Maya writes: 'The holiday was incredible. I really loved Lombok. I recommend it to everyone!' These sentences clearly show that she had a very positive experience. She does not say the holiday was boring, and she describes the hotel as cozy — not uncomfortable.

reading.question: Which sentence expresses a future plan?
options: I am going to visit my grandmother tomorrow.
I visit my grandmother every day.
reading.answer: I am going to visit my grandmother tomorrow.
reading.explanation: 'Be going to' expresses a planned future intention.

reading.question: What can you buy at a pharmacy?
reading.explanation: Pharmacies specialize in dispensing medicines and healthcare supplies.

reading.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'David called Sarah and gave _____ the book.'
reading.explanation: 'Sarah' is female and functions as an object pronoun, which is 'her'.

reading.question: What is the weather like when it is raining?

speaking.instruction: Tell a short story about a holiday you took. Describe where you went, what you did, and how you felt. Speak for about 30 seconds. Use simple past tense.

Share how you felt about the holiday and what your favourite part was.
speaking.targetSentence: I went to Bali with my family. We visited temples, went to the beach, and tried surfing. My favourite part was watching the sunset. It was an amazing holiday!
speaking.phonetic: /aɪ wɛnt tə ˈbɑːli wɪð maɪ ˈfæmɪli. wiː ˈvɪzɪtɪd ˈtɛmpəlz, wɛnt tə ðə biːtʃ, ænd traɪd ˈsɜːrfɪŋ. maɪ ˈfeɪvərɪt pɑːrt wɒz ˈwɒtʃɪŋ ðə ˈsʌnˌsɛt. ɪt wɒz ən əˈmeɪzɪŋ ˈhɒlɪdeɪ/

speaking.explanation: This storytelling task practises your ability to narrate a past holiday experience in a logical order. Start with where you went, then describe activities, and finish with your feelings. Using past tense correctly and descriptive adjectives makes your story clear and interesting.

speaking.explanation: The word 'accommodation' is important for talking about holidays. It means the place where you sleep, such as a hotel, villa, or guesthouse. speaking.explanation: This drill practises irregular past tense verbs commonly used in holiday stories. 'Go → went' and 'swim → swam' are irregular verbs that do not follow the regular '-ed' pattern. Knowing these forms is essential for telling stories about past holidays naturally.

speaking.instruction: Say the following pair of words. Notice how the syllable stress changes between the base word and the longer form. Practise both clearly.

speaking.explanation: This stress drill shows how adding a suffix can shift the stressed syllable. 'PHOtograph' has stress on the first syllable, but 'phoTOGraphy' shifts the stress to the second syllable. This pattern is common in English and is very relevant for holiday vocabulary, since we often talk about taking photographs and photography during trips.

speaking.instruction: Say the following two sentences. The first is a statement with falling intonation. The second is a yes/no question with rising intonation. Practise the difference clearly.

In English, statements about past experiences use falling intonation to sound confident and complete. Yes/no questions use rising intonation to signal that you are asking and waiting for an answer. Mastering this difference makes your spoken English sound much more natural.

questions.answer: 'We visited a beautiful waterfall and took many photos.'
questions.explanation: The first option is correct because 'visited' (past of 'visit') and 'took' (past of 'take') are both in Past Simple. The second option uses present tense, and the third uses present continuous — neither is correct for a finished holiday story.

questions.question: In the passage, Maya says 'The water was clear and warm.' What does 'was' tell us?
options: It describes how the water looked and felt in the past.
It describes how the water looks and feels right now.
It describes how the water will look in the future.
questions.answer: It describes how the water looked and felt in the past.
questions.explanation: 'Was' is the Past Simple form of 'is'. Maya is describing the water during her past holiday, not right now or in the future. We use 'was/were' to describe conditions and feelings in the past.

questions.question: Maya writes: 'I recommend it to everyone!' What does 'recommend' mean in this sentence?

questions.answer: She suggests that other people should visit Lombok because it is wonderful.

questions.question: Read this sentence: 'We explored the local market and bought some souvenirs for our families.' What are the Past Simple verbs?

questions.question: Which sentence best summarises Maya's feelings about her holiday?

questions.prompt: Write 3 to 4 sentences about a place you visited on holiday. Tell where you went, when you went, and what you saw there. Use Past Simple verbs.
questions.criteria: Uses Past Simple correctly (went, visited, saw). Includes a place name with a capital letter. Includes a time expression (last week, last year, in January). Each sentence ends with a period. At least 3 complete sentences.

questions.prompt: Describe the hotel or place where you stayed on a holiday. Write 3 to 4 sentences. Use 'was' or 'were' to describe it.

questions.prompt: Write a short holiday story (5 to 7 sentences). Use time connectors (first, then, after that, finally) to tell what you did in order. Include where you went, what activities you did, and how you felt about the holiday.
questions.criteria: Uses at least 3 different time connectors (first, then, after that, finally). All verbs about past activities are in Past Simple. Includes a feeling sentence using 'was' (e.g., 'It was amazing', 'I was happy'). Proper capitalization of place names, 'I', and sentence beginnings. Commas after time connectors. At least 5 complete sentences.
questions.sampleGoodAnswer: Last month, I went to Labuan Bajo with my family. We stayed at a hotel near the sea. First, we took a boat to Komodo Island. We saw big Komodo dragons there. Then, we went snorkeling. The water was very clear and the fish were colorful. After that, we ate fresh fish at a local restaurant. Finally, we watched the sunset from the beach. It was the best holiday. I was so happy and I want to go back again.

questions.instruction: Tell a short story about a holiday you took. Describe where you went, what you did, and how you felt. Speak for about 30 seconds. Use simple past tense.
questions.audioPrompt: Please tell me about a holiday you remember. Where did you go? What did you do there? And how did you feel about the trip? Take your time and tell me the story.
storyPoints: Tell where you went on holiday and who you went with.
Describe two or three activities you did during the holiday.
Share how you felt about the holiday and what your favourite part was.
questions.targetSentence: I went to Bali with my family. We visited temples, went to the beach, and tried surfing. My favourite part was watching the sunset. It was an amazing holiday!
questions.phonetic: /aɪ wɛnt tə ˈbɑːli wɪð maɪ ˈfæmɪli. wiː ˈvɪzɪtɪd ˈtɛmpəlz, wɛnt tə ðə biːtʃ, ænd traɪd ˈsɜːrfɪŋ. maɪ ˈfeɪvərɪt pɑːrt wɒz ˈwɒtʃɪŋ ðə ˈsʌnˌsɛt. ɪt wɒz ən əˈmeɪzɪŋ ˈhɒlɪdeɪ/
questions.hint: Use past tense verbs: 'went', 'visited', 'tried', 'was'. Describe your feelings with adjectives like 'amazing', 'beautiful', or 'incredible'.
questions.explanation: This storytelling task practises your ability to narrate a past holiday experience in a logical order. Start with where you went, then describe activities, and finish with your feelings. Using past tense correctly and descriptive adjectives makes your story clear and interesting.

Tell what the place looked like — was it big or small, old or new, cozy or modern?
Explain why you liked staying there and mention something special about it.
questions.targetSentence: We stayed at a small hotel near the beach. The rooms were clean and cozy. The staff were very friendly and helpful. I liked it because I could see the ocean from my window. It was a wonderful place to stay!
questions.phonetic: /wiː steɪd ət ə smɔːl hoʊˈtɛl nɪr ðə biːtʃ. ðə ruːmz wɜːr kliːn ænd ˈkoʊzi. ðə stæf wɜːr ˈvɛri ˈfrɛndli ænd ˈhɛlpfʊl. aɪ laɪkt ɪt bɪˈkɒz aɪ kʊd siː ðə ˈoʊʃən frɒm maɪ ˈwɪndoʊ/

questions.explanation: This task helps you practise describing accommodation using simple adjectives and past tense. Organising your description from general (type and location) to specific (details and feelings) makes your story easy to follow.

questions.instruction: You are calling Mr. Khoirul to tell him about your holiday in Yogyakarta. He will ask you questions about your trip. Answer his questions using simple past tense and describe your experiences.
questions.audioPrompt: Ring ring! Hello, this is Mr. Khoirul speaking. I heard you just came back from Yogyakarta! Tell me all about it. Where did you stay and what did you do?
questions.scenarioContext: You have just returned from a three-day holiday in Yogyakarta. You stayed at a guesthouse near Malioboro Street. You visited Borobudur Temple, tried local food like gudeg, and bought batik souvenirs. You had a wonderful time and want to share your experience with Mr. Khoirul over the phone.
questions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is your friendly English tutor who is curious about your holiday. He will ask follow-up questions about your accommodation, activities, food, and favourite moments. He speaks slowly and encouragingly.
questions.targetSentence: I went to Yogyakarta for three days. I stayed at a guesthouse near Malioboro Street. I visited Borobudur Temple and it was amazing. I also tried gudeg and bought batik souvenirs.
questions.phonetic: /aɪ wɛnt tə ˌjɒɡjəˈkɑːrtə fɔːr θriː deɪz. aɪ steɪd ət ə ˈɡɛsthaʊs nɪr ˌmɑːliəˈbɒroʊ striːt/
questions.hint: Answer each question with a full sentence. For example: 'I stayed at a guesthouse.' Use past tense: went, stayed, visited, tried, bought.
questions.explanation: This roleplay practises real conversation about holidays. Answering questions with full sentences and past tense verbs helps you communicate your travel experiences clearly and naturally.

questions.instruction: You are at a travel agency. Mr. Khoirul is the travel agent. Tell him about a past holiday you enjoyed and ask him to help you plan a similar trip. Describe what you liked about your last holiday.

questions.scenarioContext: You are visiting a travel agency because you want to go on another holiday. You had a great holiday in Lombok last year and you want to go somewhere similar. You need to tell the travel agent about your past trip — where you went, what you did, and what you enjoyed — so he can suggest a new destination.
questions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is a friendly travel agent at Happy Travel Agency. He listens carefully to your past holiday experience and asks questions to understand what kind of holiday you enjoy. He speaks in simple, clear English.
questions.targetSentence: Last year, I went to Lombok. I stayed at a beach resort. I went snorkelling and visited beautiful waterfalls. I really enjoyed the quiet beaches. Can you help me find a similar place?
questions.phonetic: /lɑːst jɪr aɪ wɛnt tə ˈlɒmbɒk. aɪ steɪd ət ə biːtʃ rɪˈzɔːrt. aɪ wɛnt ˈsnɔːrkəlɪŋ ænd ˈvɪzɪtɪd ˈbjuːtɪfʊl ˈwɔːtərfɔːlz/
questions.hint: Start by telling about your past trip: 'Last year, I went to...' Then describe activities: 'I went snorkelling.' Finally, ask for help: 'Can you help me find...?'
questions.explanation: This roleplay combines talking about past experiences with making a request. It practises past tense narration and polite question forms, both essential for real-world travel conversations.

questions.instruction: You meet Mr. Khoirul at a coffee shop. He asks about your recent weekend trip. Tell him about your short holiday — where you went, what you saw, and whether you recommend it.

questions.targetSentence: I went to Bandung this weekend. I visited a tea plantation in the mountains. The weather was cool and nice. I ate delicious street food and stayed at a small inn. It was very relaxing. I recommend it!

questions.explanation: This casual roleplay practises informal storytelling about a short trip. Using descriptive adjectives and giving a recommendation at the end makes your conversation natural and engaging.

questions.instruction: You are video-calling Mr. Khoirul from your holiday. Describe what you can see around you, what you did today, and what you plan to do tomorrow. Use present and past tense.
questions.audioPrompt: Hello! Oh wow, you are calling me from your holiday! That is so nice! What can you see around you right now? And what did you do today?
questions.scenarioContext: You are on holiday at a beach in Labuan Bajo. You are video-calling Mr. Khoirul in the evening. Today you went on a boat trip to see Komodo dragons, swam in crystal clear water, and had fresh seafood for lunch. Tomorrow you plan to go snorkelling at Pink Beach. You are sitting on the hotel terrace with a beautiful ocean view.
questions.characterRole: Mr. Khoirul is your English tutor. He is excited to receive your video call from your holiday. He asks about what you see now, what you did today, and your plans for tomorrow. He reacts with enthusiasm and asks follow-up questions.
questions.targetSentence: Right now I can see the ocean from my hotel terrace. It is beautiful! Today I went on a boat trip and saw Komodo dragons. I also swam in the sea and ate fresh seafood. Tomorrow I plan to go snorkelling at Pink Beach.
questions.phonetic: /raɪt naʊ aɪ kæn siː ðə ˈoʊʃən frɒm maɪ hoʊˈtɛl ˈtɛrəs. ɪt ɪz ˈbjuːtɪfʊl. təˈdeɪ aɪ wɛnt ɒn ə boʊt trɪp ænd sɔː kəˈmoʊdoʊ ˈdræɡənz/
questions.hint: Use present tense for what you see now: 'I can see...' Use past tense for today: 'I went...', 'I saw...' Use 'plan to' for tomorrow: 'I plan to go...'
questions.explanation: This roleplay practises mixing present and past tense in a natural conversation. Describing your current surroundings, today's activities, and tomorrow's plans is a common real-life situation when sharing holiday updates.

questions.instruction: Say the following travel vocabulary word clearly. Focus on correct pronunciation and stress.
questions.audioPrompt: Please say this travel word clearly. Think about which syllable is stressed. The word is: 'accommodation'. It means the place where you stay during a holiday, like a hotel or a guesthouse.
questions.hint: This word has five syllables: a-com-mo-DA-tion. The stress is on the fourth syllable 'DA'. Say it slowly first: a-com-mo-DAY-shun, then say it at normal speed.
questions.explanation: The word 'accommodation' is important for talking about holidays. It means the place where you sleep, such as a hotel, villa, or guesthouse. The main stress falls on the fourth syllable: a-com-mo-DA-tion. Practising long words by breaking them into syllables helps you pronounce them correctly.

questions.instruction: Say the following sentence using the correct past tense form. Pay attention to the irregular past tense verbs.
questions.audioPrompt: Please say this sentence about a holiday activity. Make sure you use the correct past tense. Listen carefully: 'We went to the beach and swam in the sea.' Now you say it.
questions.targetSentence: We went to the beach and swam in the sea.
questions.phonetic: /wiː wɛnt tə ðə biːtʃ ænd swæm ɪn ðə siː/
questions.hint: Remember: 'go' becomes 'went' in the past, and 'swim' becomes 'swam' in the past. These are irregular verbs — they do not use '-ed'. Say 'went' with a short 'e' sound and 'swam' with a short 'a' sound.
questions.explanation: This drill practises irregular past tense verbs commonly used in holiday stories. 'Go → went' and 'swim → swam' are irregular verbs that do not follow the regular '-ed' pattern. Knowing these forms is essential for telling stories about past holidays naturally.

questions.instruction: Say the following pair of words. Notice how the syllable stress changes between the base word and the longer form. Practise both clearly.
questions.audioPrompt: Listen to the stress difference between these two words. First: 'PHOtograph' — stress on the first syllable. Second: 'phoTOGraphy' — stress on the second syllable. Now you say both words. Notice how the stress moves!
questions.hint: In 'photograph', stress the first syllable: PHO-to-graph. In 'photography', the stress shifts to the second syllable: pho-TOG-ra-phy. The vowel sounds also change when the stress moves. Practise saying both words one after the other to feel the shift.
questions.explanation: This stress drill shows how adding a suffix can shift the stressed syllable. 'PHOtograph' has stress on the first syllable, but 'phoTOGraphy' shifts the stress to the second syllable. This pattern is common in English and is very relevant for holiday vocabulary, since we often talk about taking photographs and photography during trips.

questions.instruction: Say the following two sentences. The first is a statement with falling intonation. The second is a yes/no question with rising intonation. Practise the difference clearly.
questions.audioPrompt: Listen to the intonation difference. Statement with falling intonation: 'You enjoyed your holiday.' ↘ Your voice goes DOWN at the end. Now the question with rising intonation: 'Did you enjoy your holiday?' ↗ Your voice goes UP at the end. Now you say both!
questions.targetSentence: You enjoyed your holiday. ↘ / Did you enjoy your holiday? ↗
questions.phonetic: /juː ɪnˈdʒɔɪd jɔːr ˈhɒlɪdeɪ ↘/ vs /dɪd juː ɪnˈdʒɔɪd jɔːr ˈhɒlɪdeɪ ↗/
questions.hint: For the statement, let your voice fall down naturally at the end on 'holiday' — this shows you are giving information. For the question, let your voice rise up at the end on 'holiday' — this shows you are asking and expecting a yes or no answer. Exaggerate the rise and fall at first to practise.
questions.explanation: This drill practises the fundamental difference between falling intonation (for statements) and rising intonation (for yes/no questions). In English, statements about past experiences use falling intonation to sound confident and complete. Yes/no questions use rising intonation to signal that you are asking and waiting for an answer. Mastering this difference makes your spoken English sound much more natural.

practicumQuestions.question: According to the passage, how long was the flight from Jakarta to Lombok?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Maya writes: 'Our flight from Jakarta was about two hours.' This is a specific detail you can find by scanning the first paragraph of the passage.

practicumQuestions.question: Which sentence from the passage uses Past Simple correctly to describe a holiday activity?
options: 'We visited a beautiful waterfall and took many photos.'
'We visit a beautiful waterfall and take many photos.'
'We are visiting a beautiful waterfall and taking many photos.'
practicumQuestions.answer: 'We visited a beautiful waterfall and took many photos.'
practicumQuestions.explanation: The first option is correct because 'visited' (past of 'visit') and 'took' (past of 'take') are both in Past Simple. The second option uses present tense, and the third uses present continuous — neither is correct for a finished holiday story.

practicumQuestions.question: In the passage, Maya says 'The water was clear and warm.' What does 'was' tell us?
options: It describes how the water looked and felt in the past.
It describes how the water looks and feels right now.
It describes how the water will look in the future.
practicumQuestions.answer: It describes how the water looked and felt in the past.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Was' is the Past Simple form of 'is'. Maya is describing the water during her past holiday, not right now or in the future. We use 'was/were' to describe conditions and feelings in the past.

practicumQuestions.question: What time-sequence words does Maya use to organise her story? Choose the best answer.
options: 'On the first day', 'Then, on the second day', 'After that', 'On the last evening'
practicumQuestions.answer: 'On the first day', 'Then, on the second day', 'After that', 'On the last evening'
practicumQuestions.explanation: Maya uses time-sequence phrases like 'On the first day', 'Then, on the second day', 'After that', and 'On the last evening' to put her holiday events in order. These phrases help the reader follow the story from beginning to end.

practicumQuestions.question: Maya writes: 'I recommend it to everyone!' What does 'recommend' mean in this sentence?
options: She suggests that other people should visit Lombok because it is wonderful.
She warns other people not to go to Lombok.
She asks other people to help her plan another trip.
practicumQuestions.answer: She suggests that other people should visit Lombok because it is wonderful.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Recommend' means to suggest something good to other people. Maya loved her holiday, so she recommends Lombok — she thinks everyone should visit. She is not warning people or asking for help.

practicumQuestions.question: Read this sentence: 'We explored the local market and bought some souvenirs for our families.' What are the Past Simple verbs?
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Explored' is the Past Simple of 'explore' (regular: add -ed). 'Bought' is the Past Simple of 'buy' (irregular). 'Explore' and 'buy' are base forms (present), and 'local' and 'some' are not verbs at all.

practicumQuestions.question: Which sentence best summarises Maya's feelings about her holiday?
options: She thought the holiday was incredible and she loved Lombok.
She thought the holiday was boring and too short.
She was unhappy because the hotel was uncomfortable.
practicumQuestions.answer: She thought the holiday was incredible and she loved Lombok.
practicumQuestions.explanation: At the end of the passage, Maya writes: 'The holiday was incredible. I really loved Lombok. I recommend it to everyone!' These sentences clearly show that she had a very positive experience. She does not say the holiday was boring, and she describes the hotel as cozy — not uncomfortable.

practicumQuestions.question: Which sentence expresses a future plan?

I visit my grandmother every day.
practicumQuestions.answer: I am going to visit my grandmother tomorrow.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Be going to' expresses a planned future intention.
